opening.argument: The segment presents itself as a Channel 5 warning: a victim speaks out so others will not lose money, while the news graphic identifies a fake Microsoft tech-support scam. The infection warning and request for paid help are reported as claims made to the victim by purported Microsoft representatives, not as assistance offered by the program. The subsequent demand to repay an alleged excess refund with gift cards is likewise part of her account. The news presentation and BBB warning against gift-card payments reinforce the segment’s consumer-warning purpose. Nothing in that reporting establishes that the program itself solicits viewers for tech-support payments.

citations.quote: News Channel 5's Jessie Knudson spoke to a victim who said she's speaking out so others won't lose out on their cash.
This scam all started when Harriet got an email saying her computer was infected and that she needed to call a Microsoft representative at a provided number.
They asked Harriet to pay it back using gift cards, which she did
